title: ICE Exposes Massive OPT Visa Fraud, 10,000 Foreign Students Under Scanner
excerpt: Federal investigators found fake companies, empty offices, and suspicious payroll networks exploiting the popular post-graduation work program.
body:
**The Bust:** U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has uncovered what officials are calling one of the largest student visa fraud operations in American history, identifying more than 10,000 foreign students — many of them Indian nationals — working under suspicious employers through the Optional Practical Training program. ICE Director Todd Lyons described OPT as having become a 'magnet for fraud,' with investigators finding vacant office buildings, shell companies, and offshore payroll networks designed to help foreign graduates maintain legal status without performing legitimate work.

The probe, which led to 15 arrests under Operation OPTical Illusion in cities including Boston, Houston, and Washington, D.C., has resulted in over 1,000 visa revocations so far. Investigators allege that hundreds of fraudulent companies were set up specifically to 'hire' OPT students on paper, providing the employment verification letters needed to maintain F-1 visa status while the students either worked elsewhere or not at all.

**The Fallout:** The crackdown comes at a particularly sensitive moment for Indian students in America. F-1 visa issuances fell 36 percent in summer 2025, with India seeing a staggering 60 percent drop — driven in part by uncertainty around OPT's future and broader immigration scrutiny under the current administration. USCIS reported detecting 37 percent more OPT fraud cases in 2026 compared to the previous year.

For the Indian-American community, the scandal cuts both ways. Legitimate OPT participants — who form the backbone of America's tech workforce pipeline — fear guilt by association. The program has historically served as the bridge between F-1 student status and H-1B employment, a pathway that hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals have used to build careers in Silicon Valley, Wall Street, and research institutions across the country.

**The Bigger Picture:** Critics argue that OPT's self-reporting structure has always been its Achilles heel, with minimal government verification of employer legitimacy. Reform advocates are pushing for mandatory E-Verify integration and real-time employment audits. Meanwhile, immigration hawks are using the scandal to argue for OPT's elimination entirely — a move that universities warn would devastate STEM programs that rely heavily on international enrollment.

**What to Watch:** Congressional hearings on OPT reform are expected this summer. The outcome could reshape the student-to-worker pipeline that has defined Indian immigration to America for three decades.
nri_angle: OPT is the primary pathway for Indian students to transition to H-1B employment in the US; this crackdown threatens both fraudulent and legitimate participants.
author: Diaspora Desk
